title: architecture
text:
architecture

minal: Heads-up — notes from today's RFC followup. Proposing a local control plane surface per-customer VPC for on‑prem/private customers, with a regional edge-proxy fallback when peering or direct connectivity is unavailable. TL;DR: reduces blast radius + allows local routing decisions, but we need an offline cert/trust plan and an operator for signed manifests.

evan: +1 on blast-radius; main question: model routing and rollout consistency across split CPs. If each local CP can accept different manifests, how do we guarantee pinning?

jamie: we can use signed manifests with epoch/versioning. global control plane pushes signed manifest blobs, local CP verifies signer and epoch, enforces pinning. fallback proxy should be read-only for rollouts.

leo: ops question — how do we observe failover? SLIs we care about: controlplane-handshake-ms, fallback-trigger-count, model-consistency-errors. Need dashboards.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created branch spike/local-cp-edge-fallback (10 commits) — https://git.redwood/spike/local-cp-edge-fallback

minal: sketch of config (very rough):
```
controlplane:
  mode: local
  manifest:
    signer: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd
    epoch: 202603
  fallback:
    proxy: regional-edge.redwood.internal:443
    grace_period_ms: 2000
```

evan: big open: KMS/HSM access for on‑prem. We can't reach our KMS from air-gapped customers. Options: BYOK + offline signing, bring-your-root, or customer-supplied cert bundles.

jamie: agree — support BYOK + customer trust anchor. For non-BYOK, we provide an offline signing appliance workflow (signed manifests uploaded via console/cli).

leo: SRE concern: traffic surge to regional edge proxy during mass peering outage. Need circuit breakers, rate limiting, and per-tenant token buckets. Also cache KV prefixes aggressively to reduce burst.

minal: implementation notes: reuse existing relay autoscaler and token-bucket code, add 'priority' class for canaries/health-checks so we don't starve rollout telemetry. Fallback should open a TCP tunnel with TLS and keep-alive.

evan: UI/ops: console needs a 'Control Plane State' tile per-tenant showing: mode(local/remote), last_manifest_epoch, last_handshake_ms, fallback_active_since.

jamie: I'll prototype the minimal UI tile + API surface. Evang volunteer to own manifest signer docs?

evan: I'll take signer docs + offline-signer runbook.

minal: rollout plan proposal: 1) lab spike + e2e tests with simulated peering loss (this branch) 2) 1-2 pilot customers (non-critical) 3) gradual rollout with telemetry gating (model-consistency < 0.1% and fallback-rate < 1% per hour). 

leo: timeline? can we get RFC draft in 2 weeks?

minal: aim EOW for first draft; jamie + evan volunteered to co-author. Thanks — will drop diagrams in RFC PR and ping arch-reviewers.

jamie: +1, will add sequence diagrams for manifest flow and fallback path.

minal: tagging follow-ups: @jamie @evan @leo :thumbsup:
